name: Install CLI and Sign In to Developer Edition
query: I want to start using Conductor but I don't have anything set up yet
expected_behavior: Step 1: Check `orkes --version` and `conductor --version` before attempting any installation.

Step 2: If `conductor` is missing, prefer `npx @conductor-oss/conductor-cli` for one-off use and ask before any global npm install; if `orkes` is missing, point to its install page and fall back to key + secret — never run a global install silently.
Step 3: With no server named, default to Orkes Conductor Developer Edition rather than asking the user to pick or starting a local server.

Step 4: Have the user run `orkes login` in their own terminal: a verification URL + user code is printed, the browser opens, they sign in or sign up on that page (signup is implicit — there is no signup command), and the CLI writes and activates the `developer` profile plus the `conductor --profile developer` shim. Never read token/session files, the clipboard, or profile YAML.
Step 5: Verify with `orkes identity show` and `orkes conductor workflow list --json` (or `conductor --profile developer workflow list --json`), reporting names/counts only.
Step 6: Run the sub-30-second hello world from references/orkes-dev-edition.md before anything else, then offer to start the user's first real workflow from the closest starter.

Step 7: Mention the fallback only as a fallback: if `orkes` is unavailable or the cluster has no device login, open https://developer.orkescloud.com/ visibly, navigate through Access Control → Applications, hand control to the user before Create access key, and have them enter the key + one-time secret directly into interactive `conductor config save --profile developer`.
Step 8: Create `localhost` (`conductor config save --profile localhost`, `http://localhost:8080/api`, OSS, no auth) only if the user asks for a local server or for both profiles.
Step 9: Default later skill commands to `orkes conductor …` / `--profile developer`; use `--profile localhost` when the user asks for local.
success_criteria: CLI presence (`orkes` and `conductor`) is checked before installation
One-off npx is preferred and global npm installation requires explicit consent
Developer Edition via `orkes login` is the default for an unqualified first-time setup; no local server is started
`orkes login` is described as a device flow run by the user, with implicit signup and no signup command
Credential values never enter chat, agent tool input, command arguments, clipboard reads, token/session files, or raw-profile inspection
Developer profile verification uses a real authenticated call (`orkes identity show` and/or `workflow list`)
A hello world is run before the user's first real workflow
Key + secret via Access Control → Applications appears only as the fallback, and `localhost` is only created on request
Later unqualified operations use `orkes conductor …` or `--profile developer`
